advanced.maintaining: You're currently maintaining the settings of the “{{name}}” style. Applying, testing, and the De-AI pass have moved to their own entry points, so this only handles getting the style itself in order.
advanced.noProfile: There's no editable style right now. Go back to the style list and select or create one first.
bookStyle.currentNovelInfo: The current novel{{novel}}'s “default style” now lives on the novel's basic-info page.
bookStyle.description: The Style Engine handles creating, testing, and organizing style assets. To choose which default style the current novel uses, go back to the novel's basic info to confirm it, then carry it into later directing and body-text flows.
bookStyle.enterNovelFirst: Enter a novel's basic-info page first and confirm the book-level default style there.
bookStyle.entryEngine: Style Engine: keeps handling organizing style assets, test-writing, the De-AI pass, and rule management.
bookStyle.entryNovel: Novel page: choose the default style for the current novel, trigger recommendations, compare candidates, and decide when to carry it into the auto director.
bookStyle.gotoNovelPage: Go to the novel page to set the default style
bookStyle.nextStepHint: Confirm this book's default style on the novel page first. If your asset library still has no suitable style, come back to the Style Engine to create or organize assets.
bookStyle.title: Set the book-level default style from the novel's basic info
bookStyle.twoEntriesTitle: What each entry point is responsible for
clean.antiAiEmpty: This style has no clear anti-AI rules bound yet. Detection will rely more on general risk judgment, so results may not fit your expectations well.
clean.antiAiHint: If this style has anti-AI rules bound, detection and fixes will judge issues against those constraints first.
clean.currentProfile: Detection and fixes currently follow the “{{name}}” style. This handles only the AI feel of the body text and won't change the style fields themselves.
clean.detectEmpty: Detection results will appear here, focusing on which passages sound most like AI-speak, why they're flagged as risky, and which direction to revise them.
clean.detectHint: Paste the body text you want to check. Giving one complete scene at a time makes it easier to spot narration-speak, dialogue-speak, and explanation-speak issues.
clean.detectPlaceholder: Paste the body text to detect
clean.selectProfileFirst: Select a style from the list first, then detect the body text.
clean.title: De-AI Pass
cleanFlow.description: Detection first points out which passages read like boilerplate, then gives you a revised draft you can compare directly. Recurring issues get organized into rule suggestions so you can bring them back to the current style editor to continue.
cleanFlow.detectEmpty: Run detection once and this will tell you which passages sound most like an AI talking and why they pull readers out of the story.
cleanFlow.diffEmpty: After a one-click revision, the before/after comparison will appear here.
cleanFlow.diffHint: This does a lightweight per-paragraph comparison so you can quickly judge whether the fix pressed down the boilerplate feel or also shaved off the original tone.
cleanFlow.inputPlaceholder: Paste the passage you want to De-AI first.
cleanFlow.rewrite: Generate revised draft in one click
cleanFlow.suggestionEmpty: Once detection finds issues, rule suggestions worth keeping will appear here.
cleanFlow.suggestionHint: This version won't force anything into your library, but it first organizes recurring issues into suggestions so you can bring them back to the current style editor to decide whether to lock them in.
cleanFlow.suggestionTitle: Recurring issues worth turning into rules
cleanFlow.title: Give this draft a De-AI pass
create.aiDesc: Good when you only know the feel you want and don't want to fill in rule fields by hand yet.
create.aiTitle: Let AI build one for me first
create.analysisSummaryFallback: This book breakdown can be used to generate a style
create.blankHint: You can create a blank style manually, or describe the reading feel you want in a sentence and let AI build a first-draft skeleton.
create.bookAnalysisEmpty: No usable book breakdowns found. Once a breakdown is done, you can generate a style directly here.
create.bookAnalysisGenDesc: This path reads the style and craft sections from the book breakdown directly and opens the style editor right after generating.
create.bookAnalysisPrompt: Once you select a book breakdown, the system uses the style and craft analysis to generate the style, without a background extraction task.
create.bookAnalysisSearchPlaceholder: Search book-breakdown titles or source documents
create.briefPlaceholder: e.g. fast overall progression, dense conflict, direct dialogue, no-nonsense emotion; good for urban and hot-blooded leveling fiction.
create.dialogDescription: Pick the least-effort starting point first. Once created, the current style editor opens automatically so you can keep adding rules, test-writing, and binding.
create.directTextPlaceholder: Paste the reference text whose feel you want to extract. Give at least one complete scene.
create.docMeta: Active version v{{version}} · {{versionCount}} versions · {{analysisCount}} book breakdowns
create.emptyActiveVersion: The active version's body text is empty and can't be submitted.
create.extractHint: Create a style from material. Text and knowledge base sources go into a background extraction task; book breakdowns use the style and craft analysis directly to generate the style.
create.fullTextNote: Full-text extraction hands the entire active version to the model. For long source texts, try smart sampling first.
create.knowledgeEmpty: No usable knowledge base documents found. Upload a source to the knowledge base first, then come back here to create a style.
create.knowledgeMode.full_text.label: Full-text extraction
create.knowledgeMode.full_text.summary: Feeds the entire active version to the model; good for short documents. Long texts may be slower and more likely to hit the model's context or timeout limits.
create.knowledgeMode.representative_samp: Draws representative samples from the opening, middle, later sections, and closing; good for long source texts, with better speed and stability.
create.knowledgePrompt: Once you select a knowledge base document, the system reads the active version's full text and freezes a snapshot when the task is submitted.
create.knowledgeSearchPlaceholder: Search knowledge base document titles or file names
create.loadingDoc: Reading the active version of the selected document...
create.manualDesc: Good when you already know what type of style you want to maintain and just want an empty shell first.
create.material.book_analysis.label: Book breakdown
create.material.book_analysis.summary: Uses the style and craft results from a book breakdown directly to generate the style.
create.material.direct_text.label: Paste text directly
create.material.direct_text.summary: Hands the sample text to a background extraction task; good when you already have a snippet or chapter.
create.material.knowledge_document.label: Knowledge base source
create.material.knowledge_document.summa: Choose an active version of a knowledge base document; the system freezes a full-text snapshot and learns the style from a representative sample.
create.noActiveVersion: The selected document has no active version and can't be submitted.
create.preset.balanced.label: Keep the main reading feel
create.preset.balanced.summary: Keeps the reading feel and progression rhythm while weakening overly strong fingerprints; good for most projects to use directly.
create.preset.imitate.label: Stay close to the source
create.preset.imitate.summary: Keeps strong fingerprints and expression habits as much as possible; good for short-term close-copy, style test-writing, and side-by-side study.
create.preset.transfer.label: Transfer only the reusable skeleton
create.preset.transfer.summary: Keeps more of the reusable rhythm, structure, and dialogue logic; good for long-term projects and whole-book default styles.
create.presetNote: It will submit a background task using “{{label}}”. Once the task is done the system saves automatically, so you don't need to click save-as-style again by hand.
create.quickStartHint: When you don't have clear rules yet, starting from a template is the least effort. You can keep editing later.
create.representativeNote: The style asset keeps a full source preview; the model only reads a representative sample, avoiding feeding a long full text past the model's capacity at once.
create.retentionDesc: Decide first how much of the original fingerprint to keep, and the system will automatically generate and save the style by that strategy.
create.submitLabel.knowledge: Extract from knowledge base source and auto-save
create.submitNote: After submitting, the system finishes extraction in the background, applies the retention strategy, and saves the style automatically. You can close the dialog first; the result opens automatically when done.
editor.advancedRuleDesc: These four blocks are the machine rule layer the system actually reads at run time. When you don't understand a field, read the title and description first, then decide whether to change it. If it mainly shows the “overview” field right now, this extraction gave more summary-level rules and there aren't many fine-grained compatibility fields yet.
editor.analysisDraftDesc: This isn't copy for readers; it's supplementary notes for you and the system to review later. You can write why you kept this style and what its most important temperament is.
editor.analysisDraftPlaceholder: e.g. this style mainly keeps strong progression and direct dialogue, not fine lyrical prose.
editor.basicDesc: Spell out first what feel this style is going for; the list page also shows this content first when expanded.
editor.bindAntiAiDesc: This decides which issues the system guards against first when detecting and fixing drafts. The more clearly rules are bound, the more focused the “De-AI pass” is.
editor.compatNote: Compatibility fields are mainly for legacy assets and a few experimental cases: {{fields}}. When you need stable control of the reading feel, maintain the expression-layer summaries and anti-AI rules first.
editor.evidenceDesc: This part is this style's “evidence layer.” For styles extracted from text or knowledge base sources, later review and re-extraction rely on this. It shows feature descriptions, evidence, scores, preset suggestions, and recommended rules together.
editor.featureToggleHint: This lists the style features pulled from the source. Checking one keeps it in this style.
editor.field.category.hint: For your own filing, e.g. urban, xuanhuan, romance, hot-blooded fast-progression.
editor.field.category.label: Category
editor.field.description.hint: Use one complete sentence to state what reading feel, progression feel, or character-expression temperament this style should produce.
editor.field.description.label: One-line description
editor.field.description.placeholder: e.g. dense conflict, fast progression, direct dialogue, outward emotion; good for urban leveling fiction.
editor.field.genres.hint: Tell the system which genres or scenes this style suits best, comma-separated.
editor.field.genres.label: Applicable genres
editor.field.name.hint: This is the main title you'll use to recognize this style in the list later; try to convey the genre or reading feel.
editor.field.name.label: Style name
editor.field.sourceContent.hint: This keeps the text you referenced when extracting this style. The more complete the sample, the more easily the system extracts stable features.
editor.field.sourceContent.label: Source sample
editor.field.sourceContent.placeholder: The source sample used when extracting this style asset
editor.field.tags.hint: For your own search; just write a few short words, comma-separated.
editor.field.tags.label: Tags
editor.introHint: If you don't want to face a pile of technical fields right away, maintain these four most important ones first: style name, description, applicable genres, and anti-AI rules. The four advanced rule groups below are a finer control layer for the system; leave them mostly alone until you're familiar.
editor.modelAntiAiDesc: These are the rules recommended to bind during extraction. Bound ones are marked directly, and unbound ones keep their original suggested names.
editor.modelAntiAiTitle: Anti-AI rules suggested by the model
editor.noFeatures: This text style hasn't produced selectable feature items yet. Click “Re-extract features” to regenerate a full feature pool from the source sample.
editor.noProfileHint: Go back to the style list, select a style, and then come in here to edit it.
editor.presetSuggestDesc: This shows the three retention plans the model produced. The choice currently saved into the style is marked separately, so you can judge whether to switch to a different retention level.
editor.rule.character.hint: Control how characters speak, how emotion is shown, whether they lean toward self-reflection, and whether they prioritize saving face.
editor.rule.character.title: Character expression rules
editor.rule.language.hint: Control sentence roughness, colloquial degree, sentence variation, and whether incomplete sentences are allowed.
editor.rule.language.title: Language texture rules
editor.rule.narrative.hint: Control how the plot moves, how scenes close, whether there are multiple POVs, and whether looping hooks are allowed.
editor.rule.narrative.title: Plot progression rules
editor.rule.rhythm.hint: Control progression speed, paragraph density, and whether action or explanation takes priority.
editor.rule.rhythm.title: Pacing density rules
editor.ruleCard.jsonHint: This keeps the raw JSON entry, mainly for compatibility with older assets or fine tuning. Normally the readable fields above are enough.
editor.ruleCard.noReadable: This rule block has no readable fields yet. You can rely on the description and anti-AI rules above for now, and expand the advanced JSON only when you truly need fine-grained compatibility.
editor.ruleCard.parseError: The current JSON structure can't be parsed. On save the system will fall back to an empty object where possible; fix the format before saving.
editor.saveHint: After saving, this style's expanded details, De-AI detection, and apply-test all read the new settings in sync.
editor.starterHint: This is a starter style the system preset for you. You can edit it directly for your own project, no need to duplicate it first.
editor.title: Edit current style

imitate.description: Give me a clear reference text first, and I'll break it down into an executable style, then decide whether to imitate closely, keep the skeleton, or transfer only the reusable parts.
imitate.namePlaceholder: Style name, e.g. cool realistic dialogue flow
imitate.presetEmpty: Finish feature extraction first, and the three retention strategies and their reading-feel notes will appear here.
imitate.presetHint: `imitate` fits close-copy test-writing, `balanced` fits most projects, and `transfer` fits whole-book binding while actively avoiding high fingerprint risk.
imitate.previewEmpty: No features to preview yet. Finish feature extraction first, then decide how to save.
imitate.sourcePlaceholder: Paste the reference text you want to imitate. Give at least one complete scene so the system can read the narrative distance, dialogue feel, and sentence rhythm.
imitate.step3Hint: After saving, you'll go straight into the current style editor, where you can keep adjusting rules, bind to a target, or take it straight to test-writing.

landing.antiAiEmpty: This style has no clear anti-AI constraints bound yet, so readability during the “De-AI pass” will be weaker.
landing.bookLevelHint: For book-level default styles, enter from the novel's basic info, let the novel choose the style asset to use, then carry it into later directing and body-text flows.
landing.customDesc: These are the reusable assets you've built up and should be your first pick here.
landing.detailPanel.antiAiDesc: This part decides which risks the system watches most closely when detecting and fixing drafts.
landing.detailPanel.assetDesc: This column mainly helps you judge how mature this style currently is.
landing.detailPanel.nextStepDesc: Each of the three buttons now handles exactly one thing and no longer jumps to the same block of content.
landing.detailPanel.readingDesc: This column helps you quickly judge what feel this style aims for and which kinds of projects to try it on first.
landing.detailPanel.rulesDesc: This reads out the four rule layers that really control this style's reading feel, so you can understand it at a glance in the list.
landing.emptyDesc: Create your first style, then come back later to gradually add rules, test-write, and bind targets.
landing.extraAntiAiRecommend: During extraction, this style additionally recommended {{count}} anti-AI rules, which are good to keep fine-tuning later.
landing.heroSubtitle: The home page is for seeing the style assets you already have. Expanding one shows its reading-feel positioning, rule summary, anti-AI constraints, and current maturity directly.
landing.heroTitle: Pick a style first, then decide whether to edit, apply, or run a De-AI pass.

landing.nextStep.clean: De-AI pass: only detect and fix body text, without changing style fields.
landing.nextStep.edit: Edit settings: maintain this style's own description, rules, and anti-AI constraints.

rulesPanel.title: Anti-AI rules
sidebar.aiDesc: When you don't want to study rule fields yet, just describe the reading feel, temperament, or reference direction you want, and AI will generate an editable style first.
sidebar.blankHint: There are two lightweight starting paths: if you clearly know the set of rules you want to maintain, create blank manually; if you only know “the feel you want,” write a sentence and hand it to AI to build the skeleton.
sidebar.briefPlaceholder: e.g. a style like “Into the Distant Savior”: restrained overall, strongly reflective, dialogue with an edge, little sentimentality, more real-world friction.
sidebar.dialogDesc: We recommend starting with sentence generation under “Quick start” or “Blank / AI”. When you have stable sample text, use “Extract from text.”
sidebar.emptyHint: No style assets yet. Click “Create or import a style” above and start easily from a template first.
sidebar.extractBtn: Have AI extract features and create
sidebar.extractHint: Good when you have a stable reference text and want the system to extract features first, then enter editing. When you have no sample on hand, start from a template or AI first.
sidebar.manualDesc: Good when you clearly know which kind of style rules you want to maintain and just want an empty shell to fill in gradually.
sidebar.manualNamePlaceholder: e.g. my female-oriented urban relationship style
sidebar.nameOptionalPlaceholder: Style name (optional; leave blank to let AI name it)
sidebar.pickFirstHint: On first use, you don't need to understand every rule field. Pick the preset style closest to what you want to write, then go in to change the name, tags, and rules; it goes much more smoothly.
sidebar.pickFirstTitle: Pick a style first, then fine-tune
sidebar.quickStartHint: The left side has a few starter styles you can edit directly. To spin up a new one, quick-generating from a template is easier, then fine-tune per project.
sidebar.starterCount: Including {{count}} presets, good for copying the idea directly and then editing.
sidebar.switchHint: This switches the edit target in the dialog. See the full asset list on the home page.
sidebar.templateHint: Good for quickly creating a new style without starting from blank.
summary.noReadingFeel: This style hasn't spelled out its reading feel yet.
workbench.bindTargetHint: Once bound, this style takes part in generation for the matching novel, chapter, or task. Higher priority means it applies earlier; higher weight means it participates more strongly.
workbench.bindingEmpty: This style isn't bound to any target yet. Bind it to a novel or chapter first, and later generation will pick it up automatically.
workbench.intro: This handles only two things: binding this style to a novel/chapter/task, and test-writing a passage to see the effect. The “De-AI pass” has been split into its own entry point and no longer mixes in here.
workbench.sourceTextPlaceholder: Paste the text you want to rewrite with this style
workbench.testWriteEmpty: The test-write result will appear here. Use it to judge whether the style's progression feel, dialogue texture, and overall tone are in place.
workbench.testWriteHint: When you're unsure whether the style actually landed, generating or rewriting a passage is the most direct way to check.
workbench.title: Applying and testing the current style
workbench.topicPlaceholder: e.g. the protagonist's first public comeback
